payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_batch.py::test_a_stack_whose_base_branch_is_gone_refuses_its_order_without_an_abort stayed green with the spec's wrong version 'The reason names no stack base.' applied to saffron/batch.py as an edit. The claim was 'Each time a spec of the order is offered with no predecessor, `run_stack_batch` asks `stack_base_alive` about its stack base before the mint. When the branch is gone, every remaining spec on that stack base is refused. Each reason names the stack base and its branch, and the remedy, to run the next batch, which reconciles it first. Nothing more is minted, reviewed or run, no abort is counted, and the night drains. Once a layer exists, nothing asks. An order with no stack base never asks. The witness drives four arrangements. The branch is gone before the first spec, or gone after a first spec ends `EXHAUSTED`. It stays alive through every layer. The fourth order has no stack base.', and only that witness ran under the edit.
